text:
tara: quick heads-up — while QA was stress-testing fast org switches in the console, the quota tile for /console/customer/ACME briefly showed usage numbers from another org (beta-sandbox). happened 1/10 tries. :eyes:
kevin: repro steps? hosted or dedicated? any console logs?
tara: hosted. repro is: rapid clicker -> open ACME -> open usage -> switch to insights -> back to ACME. sometimes the quota graph shows ‘beta-sandbox’ id and points. here's the exact internal fetch we saw in the browser network:```
GET /internal/console/usage?panel=quota HTTP/1.1
Host: console.internal
X-Org-ID: acme
X-Route-Tag: ui/fast-switch
Cookie: session=xxx
```
response body looked fine, but the telemetry header came back as:```
X-Telemetry-Key: panel_quota:beta-sandbox:latest
```
adil: hmm. that smells like a cache key normalization bug in the shared matcher layer. if the matcher uses route-tag + panel as the cache key and drops X-Org-ID, then a cached telemetry payload could be attributed across tenants.
kevin: do we have code paths that omit org in cache keys? I know prefetch/cold-warm cache was recently refactored to use a hashed matcher key. maybe a regression in the normalizer.
tara: i dumped the matcher logs for the window and see keys like `pm:quota:ui/fast-switch` (no org) and cache hits at the same time as the UI showing wrong org.
sam: can you paste the log snippet? also any evidence that billing metrics were emitted with wrong tenant?
tara: log:```
[2026-03-19T16:02:14Z] matcher.get key=pm:quota:ui/fast-switch hit=true src=proxy-03
[2026-03-19T16:02:14Z] telemetry.emit key=panel_quota:beta-sandbox value=42 src=telemetry-worker
```
kevin: teleport: that explains the UI but the telemetry emit path looks like it used the cached payload including its original org id. if that made it to billing we have bad attribution.
ops-bot: ALERT: possible multi-tenant metric misattribution detected; affected panels=quota, sample=0.08% of requests (auto-scan), severity=medium
adil: immediate mitigation: disable prefetch/caching for quota panel or include X-Org-ID in matcher cache keys. quick patch: in matcher/key_normalizer.js change keyParts = [routeTag, panel] -> keyParts = [orgId, routeTag, panel].
kevin: agree. test plan: 1) reproduce locally 10/10 with a tiny script 2) add unit for key normalization 3) rollback safe canary (2%) with prefetch disabled if regression persists 4) run audit job to find misattributed metrics last 24h.
sam: i can cut a small canary and watch per-tenant telemetry dashboards. advise we schedule an announcement to SRE/billing after audit.
tara: disabling prefetch for quota reduced repro to 0/50 in QA. i can open a PR for the normalization change.
adil: also add defensive check: when emitting telemetry, assert that emitted orgId matches request orgId (log and drop if mismatch) — fail closed for metrics integrity.
kevin: good call. owners: @adil PR for matcher + defensive assert, @tara tests and repro script, @sam rollout and telemetry checks. i'll own the canary.
tara: noted. i'll attach the repro script and a short gif to the PR. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: incident created (INC-2026-0319) — assigned to eng-platform for follow-up and postmortem
kevin: postmortem items: root cause, full blast radius, billing impact, retro on prefetch test coverage, and a rollout checklist update for cache key changes.
adil: i'll start the historical audit and ping billing if we see misattribution. will sync in the incident thread.
kevin: if anyone sees other panels showing odd ids, drop them here — could be the matcher config is used by multiple panels.
tara: will do. thanks all.
__notes: Generated Slack thread JSON for eng-platform channel about a multi-tenant cache key normalization issue affecting telemetry and console quota panel attribution. All fields are strings or list of strings per agents.md schema.
